captions.detailed: A 3D model of a cross-slide drill-press vise, consisting of a flat rectangular base plate with integrated dovetail guide rails, an intermediate saddle, and a top jaw body assembly. The main structural frames are finished in a dark, matte black, while the sliding guide rails, screw shafts, and circular crank handles are in a contrasting light grey metal. The intermediate saddle slides linearly along the X-axis of the base, while the top jaw body slides along the Y-axis of the saddle; both axes are driven by their respective crank handles which rotate continuously on their shafts.
captions.instruction: Generate an articulated cross-slide drill-press vise model in CadQuery. The assembly must feature a base plate with longitudinal guide rails, an intermediate saddle that translates prismatically along the X-axis, and a top jaw body translating prismatically along the Y-axis, with each axis controlled by its own rotating crank handle.
captions.factory: The script uses CadQuery primitives (such as Box and Cylinder) to build the assembly parts. It defines a base part with rectangular rails, a saddle part, and a jaw body. It then defines the articulations using the ArticulatedObject class, creating prismatic joints for the sliding axes (X and Y directions) and continuous joints for the rotary crank handles on their respective shafts.
